subject: Cost/pricing follow-up: latency vs cost trade-offs and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechai.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + next steps from today's discovery: cost and latency trade-offs

Hi Alicia — great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through FintechAI's use cases. Quick recap + asks so we can build a tight cost model and pilot plan: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary product flow: real-time fraud scoring (up to ~200 qps peak), and a lower-priority batch enrichment job (nightly, ~20M tokens).
- Expected steady-state generation: ~50M tokens/month across endpoints, with spikes during business hours.
- Critical SLO: sub-200ms 95th for fraud scoring; batched enrichment can tolerate higher latency (seconds).
- Security: SOC2 required, will need details later (we'll loop security once pricing is narrowed).

Information we need from you to finalize pricing options:
1) Confirm monthly token volume range (low/likely/high).
2) Target budget range for inference (monthly run rate).
3) Any hard latency maximums for customer-facing endpoints (95th or 99th percentile).
4) Will you consider a dedicated/reserved capacity path, or do you need hosted pay-as-you-go initially?

Preliminary options we'll model next:
- Hosted API (fastest to deploy): easiest onboarding, higher unit cost but includes autoscaling; good if you want no ops overhead.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): lower unit $/1M tokens at committed volumes, predictable latency and throughput; recommended if you want consistent 95th latency and cost predictability.
- Hybrid: route fraud scoring to dedicated or edge pool with streaming + small batch sizes; route enrichment to low-cost batch instances with larger batch sizes and heavier KV caching.

Trade-offs to note (high level):
- Batch size up -> better tokens/$ but added latency. We can tune batching per route.
- Streaming / small-batch -> best tail latency but higher unit cost (more GPU kernel setup / less efficient batching).
- Caching prefixes and rerouting warm KV requests reduces token consumption and cost materially for repeat requests.

Next steps:
- Alicia: can you confirm the items above (token range, budget, SLO hard limits) by EOD Tue (10/6)?
- Marissa/Redwood: we'll prepare a 2-slide cost model + recommended tier map and an attachment with baseline pricing options for hosted vs dedicated. I'll also attach a pricing workbook you can play with.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min call Wed 10/7 to review model and agree pilot metrics.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RWI-pricing-model.xlsx (pricing workbook stub), SLO-latency-options.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps from today's discovery: cost and latency trade-offs

Alicia — perfect, thanks for the detail. I've sketched two high-level scenarios and attached the pricing workbook: hosted vs dedicated. Key calls out: 

Scenario A — Hosted (quick start)
- Unit economics: higher $/1M tokens but zero infra ops up-front. For your volume (50M/mo expected) estimated run-rate is roughly $60k–$90k/mo depending on batching and streaming choices.
- Latency: achievable 95th ~120–250ms for small prompt paths with streaming and small batch sizes; depends on region/instance mix.
- Pros: fastest to prod, lower engineering lift.
- Cons: higher variability in unit cost during spikes.

Scenario B — Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Unit economics: lower $/1M tokens at committed volumes; modeled savings 25–40% vs hosted at 50M+ tokens/mo depending on kernel optimizations and quantization profile.
- Latency: more predictable 95th (sub-150ms achievable for small prompts) with configured GPUs and streaming-friendly setups.
- Pros: cost predictability, lower unit cost, fine-grained SLO tuning.
- Cons: commit required; lead time to standing up dedicated pool if on-prem or VPC networking is needed.

Latency vs cost knobs we'll tune in the pilot:
- Batch size: increase for enrichment (saves cost), reduce for fraud scoring (improves tail latency).
- Streaming: enable for fraud route to shave tail latency (small hit to tokens/$ because fewer batching efficiencies).
- KV/prefix caching: big savings for repeat patterns — can reduce token volumes by 10–30% for your flows.
- Quantization/profile selection: mild quality trade-off vs substantial cost wins for batch-only routes.

Proposed pilot plan for Wed 10/7 call (11:00am PT):
- Walk through the attached RWI-pricing-model.xlsx live and lock in the low/expected/high token curves.
- Agree on pilot targets: 95th latency target for fraud scoring, sample traffic for 2 weeks (we can replay anonymized logs).
- Decide initial deployment: start hosted with a path to convert top throughput routes to dedicated if cost/latency require it.

I'll add a short slide with the recommended tier map ahead of the call. See attachments.

—Marissa
